source.title: Compressing Gradient Optimizers via Count-Sketches
source.authors: Ryan Spring; Anastasios Kyrillidis; Vijai Mohan; Anshumali Shrivastava

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates compressed optimizer state for memory, speed, and test performance. It does not test any listed version's claim about memorization and generalization, optimizer comparisons with SGD, or generalization gaps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out performance after compressing optimizer auxiliary variables. Those results concern optimizer compression and are recorded under fits_no_version; the study does not report training error or a training-to-test gap. Its references to large-batch training are background or citations, not its own tests.
record.test_reason: Tables 3–4 report original Momentum and Adam results on the same Wikitext-2 language-model setup: test perplexity is 94.25 versus 105.14. This bears on V4 despite the paper's focus on optimizer compression. Training-to-test gaps are unnecessary for this comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that sketching auxiliary optimizer variables exploits sparsity to reduce memory with minimal performance cost, sometimes enabling larger batches and faster training.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates Count-Sketch compression of optimizer auxiliary variables, not the memorization, architecture, regularization, or generalization-gap procedures in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance varies with optimizer state compressed and Count-Min Sketch cleaning; the Amazon experiment also changes batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Wikitext-2 optimizer-state compression produces perplexity 95.93 for Momentum, 109.24 for Adam with both moments compressed, and 106.32 with only its second moment compressed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer-state compression can preserve approximately the uncompressed optimizer's held-out performance, with losses depending on the state compressed.

fits_no_version.finding: MegaFace sketch cleaning yields 69.4% accuracy for compressed Adam versus 69.03% for original Adam; compressed Adagrad improves from 68.37% without cleaning to 69.28% with cleaning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Periodic cleaning can improve held-out performance of classifiers trained with compressed adaptive-optimizer state.

fits_no_version.finding: At epoch five on LM1B, Adam, CS-MV and CS-V reach perplexities 39.90, 40.55 and 39.88 under the adopted larger-batch recipe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compressed Adam state can preserve language-model perplexity under a common training recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: On Amazon recommendation, changing optimizer state and increasing batch size from 750 to 2600 raises Recall@100 from 0.4704 to 0.4789 and reduces epoch time from 5.32 to 3.3 hours.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer-state compression can enable faster, larger-batch recommendation training while preserving reported recall.

record.problems: The reported comparisons often change multiple recipe elements, including batch size, learning rate, model size, or compressed optimizer state. The paper does not report training error or a training-to-test gap, and gives no uncertainty estimates for the catalog-relevant test metrics.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Relative training performance, systematic tuning-budget comparisons, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and image benchmarks.

Held-out performance across small and large batches at fixed epoch budgets on image classifiers or language models. LM1B reports training-time changes across recipes but no corresponding held-out comparison.
Dropout ablations; dropout is used without a comparison establishing its effect.
Removal of memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The original record overlooks the direct uncompressed Momentum–Adam comparison relevant to V4. Conversely, it incorrectly treats the LM1B Adam table column as a batch-128 baseline. No uncertainty estimates or comparative training losses are supplied for the V4 result.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on images.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD, and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: Momentum
rows.operation_detail: Compared test perplexity after training with the original Momentum optimizer.
rows.note: Reported as the original optimizer comparison for compressed auxiliary-state methods; no training error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: Use as the momentum comparator for R3. The subject is an LSTM trained with Momentum, rather than an optimizer being a model.

source_check.locator_found: Section 7.1, Wikitext-2 setup and Table 3: original Momentum, test perplexity 94.25.

rows.subject: Momentum Count-Sketch optimizer
rows.operation_detail: Compressed optimizer auxiliary variables with Count-Sketch and trained the model.
rows.note: Compared with original Momentum; the table reports test perplexity only.
rows.check: Evaluates the proposed optimizer-state compression method against its uncompressed counterpart.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Compared test perplexity after training with the original Adam optimizer.
rows.note: Reported as the original optimizer comparison for compressed auxiliary-state methods; no training error or generalization gap is reported.
rows.check: The relevant baseline is Momentum's 94.25 perplexity in R1; Adam reaches worse perplexity, 105.14. The subject is an LSTM trained with Adam.

source_check.locator_found: Section 7.1, Wikitext-2 setup and Table 4: original Adam, test perplexity 105.14.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Sketch optimizer (CS-MV)
rows.operation_detail: Compressed both Adam auxiliary moments with Count-Sketch and trained the model.
rows.note: The text describes minor accuracy loss relative to the original optimizer; only test perplexity is reported.
rows.check: Evaluates the proposed compression method against uncompressed Adam.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Sketch optimizer (CS-V)
rows.operation_detail: Compressed Adam's second moment with Count-Sketch and trained the model.
rows.note: The paper describes negligible differences between this and the low-rank approximation; this row reports the Count-Sketch result.
rows.check: Evaluates the proposed compression method against uncompressed Adam.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Min Sketch optimizer
rows.operation_detail: Compressed Adam's second moment with Count-Min Sketch and trained the classifier.
rows.note: The text says the result slightly surpasses the baseline and closely matches its convergence rate.
rows.check: Compression and cleaning comparison, without an SGD comparator. The model is a softmax classifier on pretrained 512-dimensional FaceNet embeddings.

rows.subject: Adagrad
rows.operation_detail: Trained the classifier with the original Adagrad optimizer.
rows.note: Baseline value for the cleaning comparison.
rows.check: Misattributed subject: 68.37% describes Count-Sketch Adagrad without cleaning, not original Adagrad. The text describes the increase to 69.28% as the effect of cleaning.

rows.subject: Adagrad Count-Min Sketch optimizer
rows.operation_detail: Compressed Adagrad's auxiliary variable with Count-Min Sketch and trained the classifier with periodic cleaning.
rows.note: The text reports a 1% improvement from cleaning; it also says cleaning did not improve initial convergence rate.
rows.check: The 68.37% baseline is Count-Sketch Adagrad without cleaning, not original Adagrad. The model is a softmax classifier on pretrained FaceNet embeddings.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.operation_detail: Reported baseline test perplexity by epoch for the original Adam optimizer.
rows.note: The table reports the baseline series by epoch; the text describes batch-size scaling separately.
rows.check: Incorrect batch condition: Table 7 compares optimizer variants under the adopted batch-1024, 2048-unit recipe. Batch 128 describes the earlier recipe, without a corresponding reported perplexity series.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Sketch optimizer (CS-MV)
rows.operation_detail: Compressed Adam's first and second moments with Count-Sketch and trained the model.
rows.note: The paper reports this series alongside the Adam series; the recipe also uses a larger batch and learning-rate scaling.
rows.check: The Table 7 Adam baseline also uses the adopted batch-1024 recipe; this is a compression comparison, not a measured batch-size contrast.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Sketch optimizer (CS-V)
rows.operation_detail: Compressed Adam's second moment with Count-Sketch and trained the model.
rows.note: The text says the count-sketch accuracy is on-par with the low-rank approximation when both moments are compressed; this row records the separately reported CS-V series.
rows.check: The Table 7 Adam baseline also uses the adopted batch-1024 recipe; this is a compression comparison, not a measured batch-size contrast.

rows.subject: Adam
rows.size_stated: single hidden layer, fully-connected neural network with an embedding dimension of 1024
rows.operation_detail: Trained each meta-classifier using the baseline Adam optimizer.
rows.note: Recall evaluation down-sampled scores from 49.5 million to 1 million classes; the text separately reports a 16-meta-classifier comparison.
rows.check: Recommendation-task result outside V5's image-classifier and language-model settings; the comparison also changes optimizer state.

rows.subject: Adam Count-Sketch optimizer (CS-V)
rows.size_stated: single hidden layer, fully-connected neural network with an embedding dimension of 1024
rows.operation_detail: Compressed the second moment with Count-Sketch and increased the mini-batch size.
rows.note: The paper reports reduced epoch time alongside this result; this is not a fixed-batch comparison.
rows.check: Recommendation-task result outside V5's settings. The recipe removes Adam's first moment and compresses its second moment while increasing batch size; a fixed total epoch budget is not stated.

relationships.condition: Original Momentum versus original Adam on Wikitext-2, two-layer 672-unit LSTM, 40 epochs, batch 20, dropout 0.5.
relationships.reason: R1 and R3 report test perplexity 94.25 for Momentum versus 105.14 for Adam under their stated recipes; learning rates and clipping differ, and both use validation-triggered learning-rate decay.
relationships.display_finding: Adam achieved 105.14 test perplexity versus Momentum's 94.25%, with different learning rates and clipping and no systematic tuning search or uncertainty reported.
